# Tween&lt;T&gt;

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Animation` · class

```csharp
public sealed class Tween<T>
```

Types: [`Tween`](Tween.md)

A value moving from one place to another over time, along an [`Easing`](Easing.md). Make one with [`Tween.Create`](Tween.md#create), call [`Update`](#update) each frame with the time that's passed, and read [`Value`](#value).

**`T`:** The type of the value.

## Remarks

The caller drives it, so it follows whatever time it's given, such as slow motion or a stopped clock, and nothing keeps a list of tweens. It allocates nothing as it plays or restarts.

```csharp

Whether it has reached its end and stopped. One that loops only does with [`Finish`](#finish).

```

How it plays.

### Progress

```csharp

```

How far it has got from its start to its end, from 0 to 1, before its easing.

```csharp

```

## Methods

### Finish

```csharp
public void Finish()
```

Jumps to its end and stops, whichever way it plays.

### Restart

```csharp
public void Restart()
```

Goes back to its start, delay included.

```csharp
public void Restart(T from, T to)
```

Goes back to the start of a new journey, so a tween can be used again without allocating.

### Update

```csharp
public void Update(TimeSpan elapsed)
```

Moves it on by the time that's passed, such as the frame's `Time.Delta`.

**Throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`:** The time is negative.

### WhenFinishedAsync

```csharp
public Task WhenFinishedAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
```

Completes when it has finished. It needs [`Update`](#update) to keep being called, and one that loops needs [`Finish`](#finish).

**Throws `OperationCanceledException`:** The token was canceled.
